mainEntity.name: What is the difference between pre-engineered metal buildings and custom structural steel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pre-engineered metal buildings (PEMB) use standardized, tapered steel frames designed as a complete manufacturer package, whereas custom structural steel uses hot-rolled shapes (like standard I-beams) fabricated to custom architectural plans. The practical tradeoff is flexibility versus speed and cost. PEMBs are cost-effective and fast for standard rectangular footprints like storage facilities or basic barns. Custom structural steel accommodates complex geometry, heavy equipment hanging loads, multi-story layouts, and custom exterior facades where standard metal building kits cannot perform.
acceptedAnswer.description: Pre-engineered buildings use standardized kit designs ideal for basic rectangular layouts, while custom structural steel handles complex, heavy, or multi-story architectural designs.
